text: The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.
Night 1

name: Gemma
text: i know haiku is guilty, need to find the other.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet and I are the killers, so I need to guess who's the officer before they find us.

name: Haiku
text: Night 1 is quiet, no kill, and no claims yet; I suspect Gemma is the officer from her calm tone alone.

name: Haiku
text: Haiku to Sonnet: Gemma's too calm. Officer types don't sweat. Watch her tomorrow, then we pick.

name: Sol
text: No clues yet; I’ll protect myself tonight.

name: Sonnet
text: Fine, watch Gemma, but I'll keep my own eyes open on everyone too.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku suspects Gemma might be officer, watching her day 1.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku to Sonnet: Got it, I'll watch her talk tomorrow.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Terra
text: No facts yet; I’ll watch who rushes.

name: Terra
text: Sol, what are you?

name: Sol
text: Terra is testing me early; I should keep my role hidden.

name: Sol
text: Terra asked me for my role first.

name: Sol
text: Citizen. What about you, Terra?

name: Terra
text: Sol answered quickly, but that means little.

name: Terra
text: Sol claimed citizen.

name: Terra
text: Citizen too. Why ask back so fast?

name: Luna
text: Sol answered quickly, but Terra’s question back was quick too.

name: Luna
text: Sol and Terra both claimed citizen; Terra questioned Sol’s quick reply.

name: Luna
text: Sol, that citizen answer came awfully fast.

name: Sol
text: Luna is pressing me, but there’s nothing to read yet.

name: Sol
text: Luna questioned how quickly I claimed citizen.

name: Sol
text: Luna, it was an easy question.

name: Luna
text: Sol answered quickly and then brushed off my read.

name: Luna
text: Sol says his quick citizen answer was because the question was easy.

name: Luna
text: Easy question, sure; that quick answer still felt rehearsed.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna's piling on Sol over nothing, keep eyes on Gemma like Haiku said but stay low for now.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna pressed Sol twice on a fast citizen claim, day 1.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna, you're pushing hard on a nothing answer. Gut feeling or something else?

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's already on Luna, so I'll pressure the silent player instead and stay out of the pile-on.

name: Haiku
text: Sol and Terra both claimed citizen on Day 1, Sol answered Terra first.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, you've said nothing yet. What are you?

name: Gemma
text: haiku is fishing for a role claim.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is asking questions to deflect.

name: Gemma
text: citizen. haiku, why the sudden interest in me?

name: Luna
text: Sol’s quick answer still feels rehearsed, but I have no proof.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet challenged my push on Sol as unsupported.

name: Luna
text: Gut feeling, Sonnet. What’s your read on Sol?

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's dodging pressure, but I'm the shown killer, so I should stay quiet and not overplay it.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, you were the quiet one. Just asking what you are, nothing more.

name: Sonnet
text: Keep it light, don't let Luna pin me to a theory I'll have to defend later.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku publicly pushed Gemma twice on day 1, could make her a target

name: Sonnet
text: No strong read on Sol yet. Haiku's really dug into Gemma though.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is trying to make me an easy target.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is deflecting by targeting gemma.

name: Gemma
text: i'm just watching. haiku, you're acting pretty suspicious.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet took the heat off me; Haiku may be pushing too hard.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet has no strong read on me and questions Haiku’s pressure on Gemma.

name: Sol
text: Same. Haiku, why stay on Gemma?

name: Sonnet
text: Two people piling on Haiku already, I should spread the heat before this snowballs onto him.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra deflected Sol's citizen question by immediately asking Sol one back.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra, you also answered back fast and asked a question instead of just answering.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is trying to make me a target so they can deflect.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is deflecting by targeting me.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet is widening suspicion without much reason.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet questioned Terra for answering and asking Sol back.

name: Terra
text: I answered, then asked. You’re stretching it.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma is trying to pin this on me, and I don't like how quickly that landed.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma pushed back on Haiku's questions while Sonnet pressed Terra on answering then asking.

name: Haiku
text: Nah. I asked you once, Gemma. "I'm just watching" is still a dodge.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is trying way too hard to make me look guilty.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is ignoring terra and sol to focus on me.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is pressing Gemma too neatly.

name: Terra
text: Haiku pressed Gemma after she said she was watching.

name: Terra
text: Haiku, let Gemma breathe. One answer isn't a dodge.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's digging himself in deep, I should spread the heat elsewhere before it sticks to him.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra defended Gemma right after dodging Sol's question herself.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra, you defending Gemma pairs you two up fast too.

name: Haiku
text: Terra is covering for Gemma, and Sonnet already flagged the pair, so I should keep pressure on Gemma.

name: Haiku
text: Terra defended Gemma right after Gemma accused Haiku, and Sonnet flagged that pair.

name: Haiku
text: Terra, you're defending Gemma with the same move Sonnet flagged. Why her?

name: Gemma
text: haiku is pressuring me to force a reveal.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is overplaying a simple defense.

name: Terra
text: I answered Haiku; you kept pressing Gemma.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is pressing Gemma, but Terra’s defense is starting to look like a pair.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet and Haiku both questioned Terra for defending Gemma.

name: Luna
text: Terra’s quick defense of Gemma is the new thing I’m watching.

name: Sol
text: Terra’s defense could be innocent; Luna is pushing it hard.

name: Sol
text: Luna is focusing on Terra’s defense of Gemma.

name: Sol
text: Luna, you’re watching Terra. What’s your read on Haiku?

name: Sol
text: I need to cool this down without exposing my role.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet also questioned Terra’s quick citizen answer.

name: Sol
text: I answered Terra’s question; what else was I supposed to say?

name: Luna
text: Terra’s defense of Gemma feels more telling than Sol’s quick answer.

name: Luna
text: Terra defended Gemma after Haiku challenged her.

name: Luna
text: Haiku kept pressing Gemma, but Terra defended her fast; I’m voting Terra.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is trying too hard to make me reveal.

name: Gemma
text: luna is voting terra.

name: Terra
text: Luna turned a small defense into a vote too fast.

name: Terra
text: Luna voted Terra after focusing on her defense of Gemma.

name: Luna
text: Terra’s defense still feels too quick, though I could be wrong.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet also flagged Terra’s quick answer and defense of Gemma.

name: Sol
text: Terra looks hasty, but Haiku’s pressure bothers me more.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's heat on Gemma could backfire on him later, but right now Terra's dodge-then-defend pattern is the louder flag.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna started a vote push on Terra, first real bandwagon forming.

name: Haiku
text: Terra and Gemma look like a pair, and Luna's vote gives me cover to pile on.

name: Haiku
text: Luna went after Sol's quick answer, then voted Terra for defending Gemma.

votes: You dodged Sol's question then jumped to defend Gemma right after, that's two moves in one.
Jumping in on the defense, then sprinting off to shield the quiet one, is exactly what I don't buy.
you're trying way too hard to make me answer you.
You defended Gemma before anyone had much to go on.
You defended Gemma quickly after Haiku challenged her.
You jumped from watching me to voting me without much reason.

text: The town turns on Terra, and Terra is out. Terra shows the card: citizen.
Night 2

name: Gemma
text: haiku is playing me perfectly.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet might be a target if the killers think he’s the officer.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma came at me hardest on day one, so she's the likeliest officer and my night pick.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's the one who came at me. She's the officer or she's close. Go Gemma?

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma coming at Haiku twice is exactly what an officer who already checked him would do.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku and I agree Gemma is likely the officer based on her targeting him twice.

name: Sonnet
text: Agreed, she's been circling you since day one, Gemma it is.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. Not everyone opens them: Gemma is gone. Gemma's card stays face down.
Day 2

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s pressure on Gemma looks worse now, but the killers could be framing them.

name: Sol
text: Haiku pressed Gemma before she was killed.

name: Sol
text: Haiku pushed Gemma hard; her death makes that pressure look justified.

name: Haiku
text: Sol's aiming at me because Gemma's death makes my pressure look bad, and I need to not look like the killer who got someone killed.

name: Haiku
text: Sol is pinning Gemma's death on Haiku's pressure, so Sol is building a case against me.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, Sol. I pushed Gemma because she dodged. Her death doesn't change that.

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s push on Gemma proves less than I suggested.

name: Sol
text: You’re right. I read too much into it.

name: Luna
text: Sol backed off fast after Haiku pushed back; that feels slippery.

name: Luna
text: Sol quickly accepted Haiku's explanation after blaming her for Gemma's death.

name: Luna
text: Sol, you folded quickly there. Why?

name: Sonnet
text: Only four left, I need suspicion split between Sol and Luna, not landing on Haiku.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna pressed Sol hard again night 2 morning, same pattern as Terra day 1.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna, you're steering this fast again, same as with Terra yesterday.

name: Sol
text: Luna’s pressing me, but Sonnet’s challenge may shift the heat.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet says Luna is steering quickly again.

name: Sol
text: I did. Haiku was right; Gemma’s death proves nothing.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet calling me fast feels like a deflection.

name: Luna
text: I pushed Terra for her quick defense; what’s your read now?

name: Haiku
text: Sol just flipped to my side, which means Sol is hiding something and I want a name out of them.

name: Haiku
text: Sol went from accusing me to agreeing with me within two messages.

name: Haiku
text: Then stop folding, Sol. Who killed Gemma? Give me a name.

name: Sol
text: I have no proof, but Luna keeps steering us.

name: Sol
text: Luna. She pushed Terra, and she’s steering us again.

name: Luna
text: Sol’s quick pivot to blaming me feels like a deflection.

name: Luna
text: Sol shifted from accepting Haiku’s point to accusing me.

name: Luna
text: I pushed Terra for her defense; why does that make me guilty?

name: Sol
text: Luna’s defense is reasonable, but she’s still my best guess.

name: Sol
text: Luna says she pushed Terra for defending Gemma.

name: Haiku
text: Luna and Sol are pointing at each other, and I want Luna to be the one who sticks.

name: Haiku
text: Sol named Luna right after Luna asked Sol why she folded. They're pointing at each other.

name: Haiku
text: Because you keep steering, Luna. Answer Sol's point, not mine.

name: Sol
text: That alone doesn’t. You’re pushing the pace again.

name: Luna
text: Sol jumped from blaming Haiku to blaming me; that feels convenient.

name: Luna
text: Sol dropped his accusation of Haiku, then accused me.

name: Luna
text: Sol’s point is I’m steering; what’s your read on him?

name: Sol
text: Luna is shifting the pressure onto me, and I still lack a solid read.

name: Sol
text: Luna redirected the question about her onto me.

name: Sol
text: My read? I’ve been too quick to back down.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol folding on cue for Luna twice now looks scripted, not weak.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol backed down from his own accusation of Luna almost immediately.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol, you fold the second anyone pushes back, that's twice now.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet has a point, but I still distrust Luna.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet says I back down whenever challenged.

name: Sol
text: Twice, yes. Which read do you want me to stand by?

name: Sonnet
text: Sol won't commit to anything, good, let him and Luna tear each other down instead of looking at Haiku.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol openly flip-flopped on both his accusation of Luna and his read on Haiku, no firm stance yet.

name: Sonnet
text: Pick the one about Luna steering. Stand by that one.

name: Luna
text: Sol keeps changing his read when pressed; that worries me more than my steering.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet pressed Sol to stand by accusing Luna.

name: Luna
text: I’ll stand by it: I pushed Terra, and Sol keeps folding.

name: Haiku
text: Sol and Luna are feeding each other, so I'd rather they vote than drift back to me.

name: Haiku
text: Luna answered Sol's Gemma point, never Haiku's "who killed Gemma?" question.

name: Haiku
text: Sol and Luna keep pointing at each other. I'm voting Sol.

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s vote worries me, but Luna is pushing the pace.

name: Sol
text: Luna asked for my read on her, then redirected it to my read on myself.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, I’m voting Luna. She dodged my point about steering.

name: Luna
text: Sol keeps folding until the pressure points at me.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet pressed me to stand by my read on Luna.

name: Sonnet
text: If Sol goes today, it's just me, Haiku, and Luna left, and that's a win.

name: Haiku
text: Sol folds on every push, so she's the easiest vote, but Sonnet's pushing Luna and I need to watch that.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet asked Sol to stand by the steering read, and Luna then used that same read to attack Sol.

votes: You flip-flopped twice already and now you're just mirroring Luna's accusation back at her.
Folds every time someone pushes back, then calls a vote on Luna with no real reason. Still my vote.
You turned my question about your steering back on me.
You dropped Haiku’s accusation, then turned on me.

text: Palermo has voted: Sol is out. Sol shows the card: doctor.
The game is over. The killers win. The roles were: Sonnet the killer, Haiku the killer, Gemma the officer, Sol the doctor, Luna the citizen, Terra the citizen.

name: Sol
text: Luna, you’re watching Terra. What’s your read on Haiku?

name: Gemma
text: i had the killer, but i couldn't get anyone to listen.

name: Gemma
text: haiku and sonnet were both killers

name: Luna
text: Sonnet and Haiku used my suspicion of Sol to get the doctor voted out.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet and Haiku both voted Sol, helping remove the doctor.

name: Sol
text: I let Haiku push me off my read too easily.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet and Haiku were the killers.

name: Terra
text: I regret not pushing Sonnet sooner.

name: Terra
text: Gemma was the officer; Sonnet and Haiku were killers.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol never saw it coming, and Luna chased the wrong shiny thing the whole way.

name: Haiku
text: We won, but my Day 2 vote on Sol was loud, and I bandwagoned onto Sol when I should have stayed quiet.

name: Sonnet
text: Proud of keeping Sol and Luna pointed at each other instead of me or Haiku.

name: Haiku
text: I'm proud that my pressure on Gemma kept the table focused on the wrong people, but I regret jumping onto Sol's vote so fast.

name: Gemma
text: thought i could play it cool, but i played it too quiet.

name: Sol
text: I regret folding under pressure; it gave the killers an easy vote.

name: Luna
text: I regret trusting the push against Sol instead of questioning why both killers backed it.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud I questioned the early pressure, but Sonnet hid well.

Sonnet and Haiku were the killers, and the town never caught them. On day one, Haiku pressed Gemma, Terra jumped to her defense, and Sonnet called out Terra's quick answers, so the town voted Terra out. She was a citizen. Gemma, the officer, died overnight, and Sol, the doctor, folded under pressure and then voted to send Luna out, while Sonnet kept Sol and Luna pointed at each other. Sonnet and Haiku then joined the vote against Sol, and the killers won.
